Title: Meet the ABC's first-ever Top 5 humanities researchers - ABC News
# Meet the ABC's first-ever Top 5 humanities researchers. The winners span thousands of kilometres and undertake research into a variety of areas, including the ethical challenges doctors face, Indigenous representation in the media, and the rise of populism around the globe. *Centre for Social Research and Methods, Australian National University*. I research the what, how and why of population characteristics in Australia. My research is about the ethical challenges that doctors face in their work. I first trained as a philosopher, but now I also use qualitative research methods — in-depth interviews, for example — to learn firsthand about doctors' and patients' experiences. My research brings philosophical analysis to these experiences, with the aim of developing ethical tools and resources to support doctors in their work caring for patients. Much of my research tackles big questions about what it means to be Australian and the way that we see ourselves on screen, in the media and in literature. The work I do often involves historical research — looking through archives at the Northern Territory Library and screen archives. I also do a lot of teaching — from first year students to PhD research students. My research focuses on understanding the rise of populism across the globe. While everyone knows the obvious examples of populism — Donald Trump or, locally, Pauline Hanson — my research shows populism is a worldwide phenomenon. I've written a political history of Aboriginal land rights in New South Wales, and I'm currently working on research that seeks to contribute a better understanding of Aboriginal economies, land justice and the challenges of Aboriginal recognition. All Australians live, work, love and die on Aboriginal land. The thing I love most about being a researcher is the possibility of creating new relationships, of learning new things and contributing ideas that hopefully enable us and future generation, to live well. ***The ABC's Top 5 humanities researchers inititiative is a partnership between ABC RN and the University of Sydney. The five researchers will work at the ABC for two weeks in September.***. We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the First Australians and Traditional Custodians of the lands where we live, learn, and work.

Founded in 1947, the National Art Education Association (NAEA) is the leading professional membership organization exclusively for visual arts, design, and media arts education professionals. The National Art Education Association (NAEA) champions creative growth and innovation by equitably advancing the tools and resources for a high-quality visual arts, design, and media arts education throughout diverse populations and communities of practice. Established by Congress in 1965, the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) is an independent federal agency that is the largest funder of the arts and arts education in communities nationwide and a catalyst of public and private support for the arts. "The term 'humanities' includes, but is not limited to, the study and interpretation of the following: language, both modern and classical; linguistics; literature; history; jurisprudence; philosophy; archaeology; comparative religion; ethics; the history, criticism and theory of the arts; those aspects of the social sciences which have humanistic content and employ humanistic methods; and the study and application of the humanities to the human environment with particular attention to reflecting our diverse heritage, traditions, and history and to the relevance of the humanities to the current conditions of national life.". --National Foundation on the Arts and the Humanities Act, 1965, as amended. Created in 1972 under Congressional mandate, North Carolina Humanities is the state affiliate of the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) and one of 50+ such organizations nationally. It provides grants and humanities-based programs for libraries, museums, historical societies, schools, and other cultural and educational organizations for projects across the state that address fundamental humanities questions and create conversations about who we are and how we live together in North Carolina and the world. * A selection of Creative Arts, Social Science and Humanities-focused articles from the Research Development & Grant Writing Newsletter may be accessed when logged into your Appalachian State Google account.
